newsitem.title: USA: House panel head presses for Morris security data.
newsitem.headline: House panel head presses for Morris security data.

text.p: The head of the House Intelligence Committee accused the White House Tuesday of improperly withholding security information about Dick Morris, President Clinton's strategist until a report that he shared sensitive information with a prostitute.

In his second letter to White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta on the Morris matter, Chairman Larry Combest, a Texas Republican, said the American people had a right to know whether the Clinton administration was adequately protecting classified material that could affect national security.

Combest has asked whether Morris, who resigned August 29 as top campaign strategist, had been the subject of a background investigation, had been given a security clearance or had ever acted in an official capacity for the United States with foreigners.

Sherry Rowlands, a self-described $200-an-hour call girl, claimed in a story paid for by the supermarket tabloid Star that Morris had let her eavesdrop on telephone calls with Clinton and shown her drafts of speeches to be delivered by Vice President Al Gore and Hillary Rodham Clinton, the president's wife, at the Democratic National Convention last month.

Combest said that Panetta's failure to respond to his initial request dated September 13 for information on Morris's clearances "leads me to the unfortunate conclusion that this administration has decided for political reasons not to respond to my letter."

He said he would seek answers through other means as a member of Congress and chairman of an oversight committee in the absence of an early White House reply. The White House counsel's office did not immediately respond to a reporter's request for comment.
